answer: DeepWalk tends to outperform competing network-embedding and baseline methods (e.g., spectral clustering, modularity, EdgeCluster) when labeled training data is scarce, i.e., when only a small fraction of nodes is labeled for the downstream node-classification task. In the original DeepWalk evaluation on BlogCatalog, it kept its advantage even with as little as about 1% of nodes labeled, which is roughly 4-5 times less labeled data than the roughly 5% level at which some competitors need to match it. I am not certain of the exact percentages or margins, so treat the specific figures as approximate.
